                      [0-690] StaticText: , or Babylonian exile, was a period in

                      [0-721] link: Cyrus the Great

                  [0-685] td
                    [0-686] paragraph
                      [0-687] StaticText: The
                      [0-688] link: Babylonian captivity
                      [0-690] StaticText: , or Babylonian exile, was a period in
                      [0-691] link: Jewish history
                      [0-693] StaticText: during the 6th century BCE when thousands of Judeans from the ancient
                      [0-694] link: Kingdom of Judah
                      [0-696] StaticText: were deported to
                      [0-697] link: Babylonia
                      [0-699] StaticText: . A major deportation occurred in 597
                      [0-700] StaticText: 
                      [0-701] StaticText: BCE, following the
                      [0-702] link: conquest of Jerusalem
                      [0-704] StaticText: by
                      [0-705] link: Nebuchadnezzar II
                      [0-707] StaticText: , with further expulsions after the
                      [0-708] link: destruction of the city
                      [0-710] StaticText: and
                      [0-711] link: Solomon's Temple
                      [0-713] StaticText: in 587
                      [0-714] StaticText: 
                      [0-715] StaticText: BCE. In the aftermath of the
                      [0-716] link: Persian conquest of Babylon
                      [0-718] StaticText: in 539
                      [0-719] StaticText: 
                      [0-720] StaticText: BCE,
                      [0-721] link: Cyrus the Great
                      [0-723] StaticText: permitted the exiles to return to Judah, although many remained in Mesopotamia. The exile had a significant influence on the development of
                      [0-724] link: Judaism
                      [0-726] StaticText: and is recounted in detail in the
                      [0-727] link: Hebrew Bible
                      [0-729] StaticText: . This 1896
                      [0-730] link: gouache
                      [0-732] StaticText: painting on board by
                      [0-733] link: James Tissot
                      [0-735] StaticText: , titled
                      [0-736] StaticText: The Flight of the Prisoners
                      [0-737] StaticText: , depicts the exile of the Jews from Judea to Babylon. The painting is now in the
                      [0-738] link: Jewish Museum
                      [0-740] StaticText: in New York City.

                      [0-743] link: James Tissot

                  [0-4149] StaticText: . The university has been placed in the top 170 universities in the world by multiple central ranking tables. In addition, the UT was ranked the best technical university in the Netherlands by Keuzegids Universiteiten, the most significant national university ranking. The UT collaborates with
                  [0-5958] link: Delft University of Technology

                [0-5992] paragraph
                  [0-4172] StaticText: The university was founded in 1961 as
                  [0-4173] StaticText: Technische Hogeschool Twente
                  [0-4174] StaticText: (
                  [0-4175] StaticText: THT
                  [0-4176] StaticText: ). After
                  [0-5995] link: Delft University of Technology
                  [0-4178] StaticText: and
                  [0-5996] link: Eindhoven University of Technology
                  [0-4180] StaticText: , it became the third polytechnic institute in the Netherlands to become a university. The institution was later renamed to Universiteit Twente (University of Twente) in 1986, as the result of the changes in the Dutch Academic Education Act in 1984.
                [0-5997] paragraph
                  [0-4181] StaticText: The Dutch government's decision to locate the country's third technical university in Enschede, the main city of
                  [0-5998] link: Twente
                  [0-4183] StaticText: , had much to do with the north-eastern province's rich manufacturing industry (textiles, metal, electrical engineering, chemicals). Another important consideration was that the local economy needed a boost to compensate for the dwindling textile industry. The municipality of Enschede made the Drienerlo estate available for the first campus University of the Netherlands.

                  [0-4194] StaticText: The University of Twente was built on the former country estate of Drienerlo, situated between
                  [0-6018] link: Hengelo
                  [0-4196] StaticText: and
                  [0-6019] link: Enschede
                  [0-4198] StaticText: . The 140-hectare (345 acre) estate consists of woodland, meadows and water. Architects Van Tijen and Van Embden designed the first — and so far only — Dutch campus university along
                  [0-6020] link: American lines
                  [0-4200] StaticText: where students and staff live, work and pursue their leisure activities on campus.

                  [0-4149] StaticText: . The university has been placed in the top 170 universities in the world by multiple central ranking tables. In addition, the UT was ranked the best technical university in the Netherlands by Keuzegids Universiteiten, the most significant national university ranking. The UT collaborates with
                  [0-5958] link: Delft University of Technology

                [0-5992] paragraph
                  [0-4172] StaticText: The university was founded in 1961 as
                  [0-4173] StaticText: Technische Hogeschool Twente
                  [0-4174] StaticText: (
                  [0-4175] StaticText: THT
                  [0-4176] StaticText: ). After
                  [0-5995] link: Delft University of Technology
                  [0-4178] StaticText: and
                  [0-5996] link: Eindhoven University of Technology
                  [0-4180] StaticText: , it became the third polytechnic institute in the Netherlands to become a university. The institution was later renamed to Universiteit Twente (University of Twente) in 1986, as the result of the changes in the Dutch Academic Education Act in 1984.
                [0-5997] paragraph
                  [0-4181] StaticText: The Dutch government's decision to locate the country's third technical university in Enschede, the main city of
                  [0-5998] link: Twente
                  [0-4183] StaticText: , had much to do with the north-eastern province's rich manufacturing industry (textiles, metal, electrical engineering, chemicals). Another important consideration was that the local economy needed a boost to compensate for the dwindling textile industry. The municipality of Enschede made the Drienerlo estate available for the first campus University of the Netherlands.

                [0-6017] paragraph
                  [0-4194] StaticText: The University of Twente was built on the former country estate of Drienerlo, situated between
                  [0-6018] link: Hengelo
                  [0-4196] StaticText: and
                  [0-6019] link: Enschede
                  [0-4198] StaticText: . The 140-hectare (345 acre) estate consists of woodland, meadows and water. Architects Van Tijen and Van Embden designed the first — and so far only — Dutch campus university along
                  [0-6020] link: American lines
                  [0-4200] StaticText: where students and staff live, work and pursue their leisure activities on campus.

                [0-6026] paragraph
                  [0-4204] StaticText: The Student Union, which is run entirely by students, manages several premises, including the student social centre (De Pakkerij) and study centre (Wallstreet) in Enschede and The Water sports complex on the

                [0-6044] paragraph
                  [0-4215] StaticText: According to the

                [0-6136] paragraph
                  [0-4267] StaticText: In the Shanghai Ranking 2021, the University of Twente's Geoinformation and Earth Observation Sciences were awarded. In the field of remote sensing, the university landed among the top ten universities in the world.
                  [0-6137] superscript
                    [0-6138] link: [15]
                      [0-6139] span
                        [0-4268] StaticText: [
                        [0-4269] StaticText: 15
                        [0-4270] StaticText: ]
                  [0-4271] StaticText: The commitment in this area will be further expanded in the coming years.
                  [0-6142] superscript
                    [0-6143] link: [16]
                      [0-6144] span
                        [0-4272] StaticText: [
                        [0-4273] StaticText: 16
                        [0-4274] StaticText: ]
                [0-6147] paragraph
                  [0-4275] StaticText: According to Keuzegids Universiteiten, the most significant national university ranking, the University of Twente is the best technical university in the Netherlands.

                    [0-6166] link: edit
                  [0-6169] paragraph
                    [0-4287] StaticText: The current rector magnificus of the university is professor Tom Veldkamp. The other two members of the executive board are Vinod Subramaniam (president of the executive board) and Machteld Roos (vice-president)
                    [0-6170] superscript
                      [0-6171] link: [18]
                        [0-6172] span

                [0-6175] region: Faculties

                    [0-5240] link: edit
                  [0-6182] paragraph
                    [0-4295] StaticText: There are five faculties at the University of Twente; each faculty is in turn organized into several departments:
                  [0-6183] list
                    [0-6184] listitem
                      [0-4296] ListMarker: •
                      [0-4297] StaticText: Behavioural, Management and Social Sciences (BMS) – i.a. Communication studies, psychology, public administration, educational science & technology, European studies, environmental & energy management and Risk management
                    [0-6185] listitem
                      [0-4298] ListMarker: •
                      [0-4299] StaticText: Engineering Technology (ET) – i.a. Mechanical engineering, civil engineering, industrial design engineering and
                      [0-6186] link: sustainable energy
                      [0-4301] StaticText: technology.
                    [0-6187] listitem
                      [0-4302] ListMarker: •
                      [0-4303] StaticText: Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science (EEMCS) – i.a. Electrical engineering, applied mathematics, interaction technology, internet science & Technology and computer science.
                    [0-6188] listitem
                      [0-4304] ListMarker: •
                      [0-4305] StaticText: Technische Natuurwetenschappen (TNW)
                      [0-4306] StaticText: 
                      [0-4307] StaticText: : Applied Natural Science and Technology – i.a. Chemical engineering, applied physics, biomedical engineering, health sciences, advanced technology and nanotechnology.
                    [0-6190] listitem
                      [0-4308] ListMarker: •
                      [0-6191] link: Faculty of Geo-information Sciences and Earth Observation
                      [0-4310] StaticText: (ITC) – i.a. spatial engineering, cartography, geo-information science & earth observation.
                  [0-6192] paragraph
                    [0-4311] StaticText: Next to the programmes administered by the faculties mentioned above, University College Twente offers the broad honours BSc programme in Technology and Liberal Arts and Sciences, or ATLAS for short, and the Twente Graduate School offers post graduate education (PhD and PDEng).
                    [0-6193] superscript
                      [0-6194] link: [19]
                        [0-6195] span
                          [0-4312] StaticText: [
                          [0-4313] StaticText: 19
                          [0-4314] StaticText: ]
                    [0-4315] StaticText: Since 2019, this study is part of the faculty ITC.

                  [0-5955] link: public

                  [0-5956] link: technical university
                  [0-4147] StaticText: located in
                  [0-5957] link: Enschede, Netherlands
                  [0-4149] StaticText: . The university has been placed in the top 170 universities in the world by multiple central ranking tables. In addition, the UT was ranked the best technical university in the Netherlands by Keuzegids Universiteiten, the most significant national university ranking. The UT collaborates with
                  [0-5958] link: Delft University of Technology
                  [0-4151] StaticText: ,
                  [0-5959] link: Eindhoven University of Technology
                  [0-4153] StaticText: and the
                  [0-5960] link: Wageningen University and Research Centre
                  [0-4155] StaticText: under the umbrella of
                  [0-5961] link: 4TU
                  [0-4157] StaticText: and is also a partner in the
                  [0-5962] link: European Consortium of Innovative Universities
                  [0-4159] StaticText: (ECIU).

                [0-5992] paragraph
                  [0-4172] StaticText: The university was founded in 1961 as
                  [0-4173] StaticText: Technische Hogeschool Twente
                  [0-4174] StaticText: (
                  [0-4175] StaticText: THT
                  [0-4176] StaticText: ). After
                  [0-5995] link: Delft University of Technology
                  [0-4178] StaticText: and
                  [0-5996] link: Eindhoven University of Technology
                  [0-4180] StaticText: , it became the third polytechnic institute in the Netherlands to become a university. The institution was later renamed to Universiteit Twente (University of Twente) in 1986, as the result of the changes in the Dutch Academic Education Act in 1984.
                [0-5997] paragraph
                  [0-4181] StaticText: The Dutch government's decision to locate the country's third technical university in Enschede, the main city of
                  [0-5998] link: Twente
                  [0-4183] StaticText: , had much to do with the north-eastern province's rich manufacturing industry (textiles, metal, electrical engineering, chemicals). Another important consideration was that the local economy needed a boost to compensate for the dwindling textile industry. The municipality of Enschede made the Drienerlo estate available for the first campus University of the Netherlands.

                [0-6017] paragraph
                  [0-4194] StaticText: The University of Twente was built on the former country estate of Drienerlo, situated between
                  [0-6018] link: Hengelo
                  [0-4196] StaticText: and
                  [0-6019] link: Enschede
                  [0-4198] StaticText: . The 140-hectare (345 acre) estate consists of woodland, meadows and water. Architects Van Tijen and Van Embden designed the first — and so far only — Dutch campus university along
                  [0-6020] link: American lines
                  [0-4200] StaticText: where students and staff live, work and pursue their leisure activities on campus.

                [0-5992] paragraph
                  [0-4172] StaticText: The university was founded in 1961 as
                  [0-4173] StaticText: Technische Hogeschool Twente
                  [0-4174] StaticText: (
                  [0-4175] StaticText: THT
                  [0-4176] StaticText: ). After
                  [0-5995] link: Delft University of Technology
                  [0-4178] StaticText: and
                  [0-5996] link: Eindhoven University of Technology
                  [0-4180] StaticText: , it became the third polytechnic institute in the Netherlands to become a university. The institution was later renamed to Universiteit Twente (University of Twente) in 1986, as the result of the changes in the Dutch Academic Education Act in 1984.
                [0-5997] paragraph
                  [0-4181] StaticText: The Dutch government's decision to locate the country's third technical university in Enschede, the main city of
                  [0-5998] link: Twente
                  [0-4183] StaticText: , had much to do with the north-eastern province's rich manufacturing industry (textiles, metal, electrical engineering, chemicals). Another important consideration was that the local economy needed a boost to compensate for the dwindling textile industry. The municipality of Enschede made the Drienerlo estate available for the first campus University of the Netherlands.

                [0-6017] paragraph
                  [0-4194] StaticText: The University of Twente was built on the former country estate of Drienerlo, situated between
                  [0-6018] link: Hengelo
                  [0-4196] StaticText: and
                  [0-6019] link: Enschede
                  [0-4198] StaticText: . The 140-hectare (345 acre) estate consists of woodland, meadows and water. Architects Van Tijen and Van Embden designed the first — and so far only — Dutch campus university along
                  [0-6020] link: American lines
                  [0-4200] StaticText: where students and staff live, work and pursue their leisure activities on campus.
                  [0-6021] superscript
                    [0-6022] link: [5]

                        [0-4203] StaticText: ]

                  [0-6027] link: Twentekanaal

                [0-6044] paragraph
                  [0-4215] StaticText: According to the
                  [0-6045] link: Times Higher Education Ranking
                  [0-4217] StaticText: , the University of Twente is considered one of the 200 most prestigious universities globally.

                        [0-4219] StaticText: 7
                        [0-4220] StaticText: ]
                  [0-4221] StaticText: The university performed particularly strongly in the Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure 2021 ranking. Here, the university was ranked eleventh in the world rankings.

                [0-6136] paragraph
                  [0-4267] StaticText: In the Shanghai Ranking 2021, the University of Twente's Geoinformation and Earth Observation Sciences were awarded. In the field of remote sensing, the university landed among the top ten universities in the world.

                    [0-6138] link: [15]

                  [0-4271] StaticText: The commitment in this area will be further expanded in the coming years.

                [0-6147] paragraph

                  [0-6169] paragraph
                    [0-4287] StaticText: The current rector magnificus of the university is professor Tom Veldkamp. The other two members of the executive board are Vinod Subramaniam (president of the executive board) and Machteld Roos (vice-president)
                    [0-6170] superscript

                    [0-5240] link: edit
                  [0-6182] paragraph
                    [0-4295] StaticText: There are five faculties at the University of Twente; each faculty is in turn organized into several departments:
                  [0-6183] list
                    [0-6184] listitem
                      [0-4296] ListMarker: •
                      [0-4297] StaticText: Behavioural, Management and Social Sciences (BMS) – i.a. Communication studies, psychology, public administration, educational science & technology, European studies, environmental & energy management and Risk management
                    [0-6185] listitem
                      [0-4298] ListMarker: •
                      [0-4299] StaticText: Engineering Technology (ET) – i.a. Mechanical engineering, civil engineering, industrial design engineering and
                      [0-6186] link: sustainable energy
                      [0-4301] StaticText: technology.
                    [0-6187] listitem
                      [0-4302] ListMarker: •
                      [0-4303] StaticText: Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science (EEMCS) – i.a. Electrical engineering, applied mathematics, interaction technology, internet science & Technology and computer science.
                    [0-6188] listitem
                      [0-4304] ListMarker: •
                      [0-4305] StaticText: Technische Natuurwetenschappen (TNW)
                      [0-4306] StaticText: 
                      [0-4307] StaticText: : Applied Natural Science and Technology – i.a. Chemical engineering, applied physics, biomedical engineering, health sciences, advanced technology and nanotechnology.
                    [0-6190] listitem
                      [0-4308] ListMarker: •
                      [0-6191] link: Faculty of Geo-information Sciences and Earth Observation
                      [0-4310] StaticText: (ITC) – i.a. spatial engineering, cartography, geo-information science & earth observation.
                  [0-6192] paragraph
                    [0-4311] StaticText: Next to the programmes administered by the faculties mentioned above, University College Twente offers the broad honours BSc programme in Technology and Liberal Arts and Sciences, or ATLAS for short, and the Twente Graduate School offers post graduate education (PhD and PDEng).
                    [0-6193] superscript
                      [0-6194] link: [19]
                        [0-6195] span
                          [0-4312] StaticText: [
                          [0-4313] StaticText: 19
                          [0-4314] StaticText: ]
                    [0-4315] StaticText: Since 2019, this study is part of the faculty ITC.

                [0-5992] paragraph
                  [0-4172] StaticText: The university was founded in 1961 as
                  [0-4173] StaticText: Technische Hogeschool Twente
                  [0-4174] StaticText: (
                  [0-4175] StaticText: THT
                  [0-4176] StaticText: ). After
                  [0-5995] link: Delft University of Technology
                  [0-4178] StaticText: and
                  [0-5996] link: Eindhoven University of Technology
                  [0-4180] StaticText: , it became the third polytechnic institute in the Netherlands to become a university. The institution was later renamed to Universiteit Twente (University of Twente) in 1986, as the result of the changes in the Dutch Academic Education Act in 1984.
                [0-5997] paragraph
                  [0-4181] StaticText: The Dutch government's decision to locate the country's third technical university in Enschede, the main city of
                  [0-5998] link: Twente
                  [0-4183] StaticText: , had much to do with the north-eastern province's rich manufacturing industry (textiles, metal, electrical engineering, chemicals). Another important consideration was that the local economy needed a boost to compensate for the dwindling textile industry. The municipality of Enschede made the Drienerlo estate available for the first campus University of the Netherlands.

                [0-6017] paragraph
                  [0-4194] StaticText: The University of Twente was built on the former country estate of Drienerlo, situated between
                  [0-6018] link: Hengelo
                  [0-4196] StaticText: and
                  [0-6019] link: Enschede
                  [0-4198] StaticText: . The 140-hectare (345 acre) estate consists of woodland, meadows and water. Architects Van Tijen and Van Embden designed the first — and so far only — Dutch campus university along
                  [0-6020] link: American lines
                  [0-4200] StaticText: where students and staff live, work and pursue their leisure activities on campus.
